documents.title: Godel's Letter to von Neumann (March 20, 1956)
documents.author: Kurt Godel
documents.summary: The famous letter in which Godel asks von Neumann whether the provability of a formula of length N can be decided in polynomial time -- the earliest known formulation of what became the P vs NP problem.
documents.egpt_relevance: Direct origin of the P vs NP question. Godel asks whether phi(N) grows polynomially or exponentially -- the exact question EGPT claims to resolve. This letter is the historical anchor for the entire repository.
judgement_calls: Original PDF could not be directly parsed due to filename encoding. Text reconstructed from the well-known published version in Godel's Collected Works, Vol. V.
The exact mathematical notation (e.g., phi(N), KN^2) may vary slightly from the original manuscript.

documents.title: Von Neumann: Letters to K. Godel (Combined)
documents.author: John von Neumann
documents.summary: Combined compilation of all four von Neumann letters to Godel. Covers the discovery of the second incompleteness theorem, the intuitionism debate, and the IAS invitation. Individual letters also available as separate files.
documents.egpt_relevance: The von Neumann-Godel correspondence is the historical model for the EGPT debate system. The disagreement on formalizability of intuitionism (Letter 3) directly motivates EGPT's thesis that constructive mathematics can be fully formalized.
judgement_calls: Letter 3 contains a duplicate closing ('I remain with best wishes...' and 'Yours sincerely') -- this appears to be how the source text transitions between sections in the combined volume.

documents.title: Von Neumann to Godel, November 20, 1930
documents.author: John von Neumann
documents.summary: Von Neumann announces his independent discovery of what became known as Godel's second incompleteness theorem: the consistency of mathematics is unprovable within the system. He asks Godel about 'translatability' of intuitionistic proofs into formal systems.
documents.egpt_relevance: Documents the moment when the unprovability of consistency was independently discovered. The 'translatability' question -- whether intuitionistic constructions can be captured formally -- is the precursor to EGPT's thesis that all constructive mathematics is formalizable.
judgement_calls: The footnote number 73 matches the published source. The archival attribution is preserved verbatim.

documents.title: Von Neumann to Godel, November 29, 1930
documents.author: John von Neumann
documents.summary: Von Neumann graciously defers to Godel's priority on the second incompleteness theorem. He draws the strong conclusion that 'there is no rigorous justification for classical mathematics' and argues that all intuitionistic reasoning can be formally captured via transfinite recursions.
documents.egpt_relevance: Von Neumann's claim that every intuitionistic consideration can be formally copied via transfinite recursions up to ordinals of the second number class is a direct precursor to EGPT's thesis. His conclusion about foundations anticipates the information-theoretic resolution.
judgement_calls: The mathematical notation W -> A in 'You proved W -> A' is preserved as in the published translation.

documents.title: Von Neumann to Godel, January 12, 1931
documents.author: John von Neumann
documents.summary: The pivotal letter. Von Neumann (1) announces a decision method for propositional provability, (2) 'absolutely disagrees' with Godel on formalizability of intuitionism, (3) challenges Godel to name a single intuitionistic construction that cannot be formalized in system A, and (4) sketches a simplified proof of the second incompleteness theorem.
documents.egpt_relevance: The most EGPT-relevant letter. Von Neumann's challenge -- 'name a single construction that cannot be formalized' -- is the exact challenge EGPT answers constructively. His decision method for provability anticipates complexity-theoretic questions. The debate on intuitionism is the historical model for the @pnp-godel vs @pnp-jvm debate agents.
judgement_calls: The address shows 'Hohenzollerstrasse' (one 'n') which matches the PDF scan. This may be a variant spelling or transcription artifact vs. 'Hohenzollernstrasse' in Letter 1.
The mathematical argument in steps (1)-(4) uses the tilde symbol for logical equivalence and arrow for implication, matching the published source.
The image file 'JvM Letter to Godel Intuitionist.png' shows the first page of this letter's English translation.

documents.title: Von Neumann to Godel, February 14, 1933
documents.author: John von Neumann
documents.summary: A warm personal letter from Budapest. Von Neumann has just returned from Princeton, mentions his new position at the IAS, and invites Godel to visit. He offers to provide information about the Institute on Veblen's request.
documents.egpt_relevance: Documents the personal relationship between the two central figures of the EGPT debate model. Shows von Neumann's role in bringing Godel to the IAS, where both would spend the rest of their careers.
judgement_calls: The address 'Arany Janos utca 16' is von Neumann's family home in Budapest. The 'V' refers to the 5th district of Budapest.

documents.title: Introductory Comments (Complete Index)
documents.author: Miklos Redei (editor)
documents.summary: Index file linking to all nine sections of the Introductory Comments. Provides a thematic overview of von Neumann's work as revealed through his correspondence.
documents.egpt_relevance: Provides the scholarly context for understanding the von Neumann-Godel correspondence. Sections 2 (Logic), 6 (Quantum Logic), and 8 (Computer Science) are most directly relevant to EGPT.
judgement_calls: The complete PDF could not be read due to missing poppler-utils. Content reconstructed from individual section PDFs and the document images provided during conversion.

documents.title: Section 1: Von Neumann's Life and Career in Light of His Letters
documents.author: Miklos Redei (editor)
documents.summary: Biographical overview covering von Neumann's Budapest childhood, education at ETH Zurich, move to Princeton, marriage, wartime work including the Manhattan Project, honors, consulting career, appointment as Atomic Energy Commissioner, and death in 1957.
documents.egpt_relevance: Background on von Neumann's character and working style. His role as both pure mathematician and applied scientist mirrors EGPT's thesis that theory and computation are unified.
judgement_calls: Some letter dates marked with [????] in the original indicate uncertain dating by the editor.
Quotations from letters are preserved as given in the published source.

documents.title: Section 2: Logic and Foundations of Mathematics
documents.author: Miklos Redei (editor)
documents.summary: Covers the Konigsberg conference, von Neumann's independent discovery of the second incompleteness theorem, his immediate grasp of its implications, his disagreement with Godel on intuitionism, and his efforts to bring Godel to safety in America.
documents.egpt_relevance: Core EGPT-relevant section. Documents the foundational debate that EGPT's proof architecture models. Von Neumann's interpretation that 'there is no rigorous justification for classical mathematics' and Godel's counterposition frame the entire P=NP debate.

documents.title: Section 3: Operator Algebras
documents.author: Miklos Redei (editor)
documents.summary: The Murray-von Neumann classification of factors (types I through III), the dimension function, the discovery of type III-infinity factors, and the group measure space construction technique.
documents.egpt_relevance: The classification of von Neumann algebras by dimension function values (integers, reals, or {0,infinity}) is structurally analogous to EGPT's classification of information spaces by entropy. The type II_1 factor with its continuous dimension function [0,1] connects to EGPT's treatment of the continuum.
judgement_calls: Mathematical notation for factor types uses subscripts matching the published source.

documents.title: Section 4: Unbounded Operators
documents.author: Miklos Redei (editor)
documents.summary: Technical section on the theory of unbounded operators: symmetric vs. selfadjoint operators, defect indices, the spectral theorem, and the Hamilton operator selfadjointness problem resolved by Kato in 1951.
documents.egpt_relevance: The spectral theorem and operator domain issues connect to EGPT's treatment of observables in information space. The distinction between symmetric and selfadjoint operators (von Neumann's terminology: 'Hermitean' vs 'hypermaximal') reflects domain-sensitivity that parallels EGPT's careful treatment of computability domains.
judgement_calls: Von Neumann's letter to Kemble is dated 'December 6, [????]' -- the year is uncertain, estimated as 1935 by the editor.

documents.title: Section 5: Quantum Mechanics
documents.author: Miklos Redei (editor)
documents.summary: Covers five subsections: mathematical foundations of Hilbert space QM, the Stone-von Neumann uniqueness theorem for canonical commutation relations, the EPR paper and quantum correlations, and relativistic QM including von Neumann's spacetime quantization scheme.
documents.egpt_relevance: Von Neumann's spacetime quantization (discrete space, continuous time, Lorentz-invariant) anticipates EGPT's discrete information space. His operator P = (1/2pi)A as a projection in the CCR uniqueness proof connects to EGPT's use of projections as information-theoretic primitives. The EPR discussion shows von Neumann treating correlations as informational rather than physical -- consistent with EGPT's 'address is the map' principle.
judgement_calls: The Weyl-form equations (12)-(15) and the Schrodinger representation (16) are transcribed directly from the PDF.
Von Neumann's spacetime quantization spectrum description (items 1-6) is transcribed from his letter to Ortvay.

documents.title: Section 6: Quantum Logic
documents.author: Miklos Redei (editor)
documents.summary: The Birkhoff-von Neumann paper on quantum logic (1936); Boolean algebra and classical logic; orthomodularity vs. modularity vs. distributivity; the choice between two definitions of 'join' for quantum propositional systems; connections between quantum logic and intuitionism.
documents.egpt_relevance: Highly relevant. Von Neumann's observation that quantum logic exhibits features reminiscent of intuitionistic logic connects directly to the von Neumann-Godel debate on intuitionism. The non-Boolean lattice structure of quantum propositions parallels EGPT's treatment of information spaces where classical logic does not fully apply. The orthomodularity condition is structurally related to EGPT's entropy constraints.
judgement_calls: The PDF for this section (11 pages) could not be fully read due to missing poppler-utils. Content reconstructed from the IntroductoryComments_Complete PDF pages and from the individual section PDFs that were readable.
The detailed technical arguments from von Neumann's letters to Birkhoff about subspace lattice properties are summarized rather than transcribed in full due to source accessibility constraints.

documents.title: Section 7: Ergodic Theorem
documents.author: Miklos Redei (editor)
documents.summary: Von Neumann's mean ergodic theorem (1931), the priority dispute with G.D. Birkhoff, the distinction between ergodicity and quasi-ergodicity, and the physical significance for statistical mechanics.
documents.egpt_relevance: The ergodic theorem's statement that time averages equal space averages (under ergodicity) connects to EGPT's principle that the address is the map: in an ergodic system, knowing the trajectory (address) gives you the phase-space average (map). Von Neumann's emphasis that 'all disorder assumptions are implied by the single hypothesis' anticipates EGPT's maximal compression principle.

documents.title: Section 8: Computer Science
documents.author: Miklos Redei (editor)
documents.summary: Von Neumann's computer work: origins in WWII numerical computation, ENIAC and EDVAC, the 'First Draft' report, the IAS computer project, universal machines, computational complexity intuitions, the Monte Carlo method, and three concerns about computing culture.
documents.egpt_relevance: Directly relevant. Von Neumann's letter to McKinsey distinguishing 'mathematical-analytical' problems (low logical type) from 'logical-combinatorial' problems (high logical type) anticipates the P vs NP distinction. His insistence on building machines for 'experimentation' rather than 'specific problems' parallels EGPT's approach. His concern about 'deformed' machines lacking proper balance between functions mirrors EGPT's thesis about FLOPs vs IOPs.
judgement_calls: Von Neumann's quote about 'obscene interest in computation' is attributed to a letter to Veblen (May 21, 1943) not included in the Selected Letters volume but quoted by Aspray.

documents.title: Section 9: Game Theory
documents.author: Miklos Redei (editor)
documents.summary: The Minimax Theorem (1928), Theory of Games and Economic Behavior with Morgenstern, priority dispute with Frechet over Borel, utility theory, and chess combinatorics.
documents.egpt_relevance: The Minimax Theorem's existence proof for mixed strategies (without constructing them) parallels classical existence proofs in complexity theory. Von Neumann's estimate of 10^80 valid chess games and his observation that one can prove a winning strategy exists without knowing it connects to EGPT's information-theoretic treatment of NP problems.

related_files.image_description: Scan of the first page of the English translation of von Neumann's January 12, 1931 letter to Godel (Letter 3). Shows the Berlin address, salutation, and the key passage on omega-consistency, the decision method for propositional provability, and the beginning of the disagreement on intuitionism.
